report:
Fresh final followup review of crate_ownership. Saved/read the previous complete report and captures, started fresh, recaptured all three helper dependencies, and compared every fragment. Claim, all three tests, four of five implementation files and all helpers are unchanged. The only spec.rs delta is an implementation_references association comment on an unrelated validator. Ownership, identity and publication behavior are unchanged.

The complete claim requires each Sage chapter to have a manifest-established modeled Rust crate boundary, ownership checked against the Rust workspace, and preserved compiler-model identities when only book directory placement changes. All five ordinary implementation entries remain relevant. workspace::crate_source_owner selects the deepest enclosing manifest directory; document_namespace uses the modeled crate name/module header instead of directory spelling. validate::build_model enforces crate.sage manifests, unique crates, nearest-owner/module-path consistency and modeled declaration identities. spec::load_workspace rejects Sage chapters without model ownership, while keeping path-derived chapter namespace separate from model identity. book::generate_crates validates model and Cargo correspondence before publishing the explorer. correspondence::validate requires Rust mappings and rejects wrong-crate ownership; Cargo metadata supplies actual crate/target owners. Browser serialization obtains the same modeled namespaces, while navigation routes use current source paths. The added comment changes none of these checks.

All three ordinary tests were reassessed. orphan_sage_module_and_nonexistent_rust_crate_are_rejected separately adds an orphan module and an unmapped missing crate manifest, requiring failure, relevant diagnostics, no output and no published asset. The missing-crate substring is broad but its fixture isolates that new unmapped manifest. invalid_models_and_correspondence_fail_before_publishing_an_explorer covers unknown modeled type, missing mappings and an explicitly wrong-crate mapping; it requires the expected error and no publication in each case. relocating_crate_sources_preserves_model_identity_and_updates_book_routes generates a baseline, moves demo to compiler/frontend without changing modeled paths, regenerates and asserts new chapter paths/absence of old paths, unchanged exact model namespace and declaration-ID sets, unchanged Rust mapping with concrete ActualItem identity, updated navigation/output route and increased relative explorer path. The cross-crate support reference remains validated after relocation. These are substantive before/after assertions distinguishing book placement from Rust identity.

Captured fixture helpers write real two-package Cargo/model/book sources, invoke the real preprocessor, parse JSON/snapshot data and recursively reject duplicate chapter paths. All claim requirements have current ordinary code and meaningful positive/negative/relocation evidence; there are no TODO/N/A entries or deferrals. The actual marker-only delta was checked against the full prior assessment and no other relied-on content changed. No source edits, build or behavioral tests occurred in this review; fresh start/read/record and source inspection only. No requested edits.
